entries.title: Psalms 76:1
segments: The reference of this psalm to the overthrow of Sennacherib's army cannot be mistaken.  See the history,
. As to the title Asaph, see introductory note to

. 
 
God is known only in those lands which are enlightened by revelation; all others are veiled in darkness and the shadow of death.  Hence, those who are blessed with the word of God should communicate it to all people.

entries.title: Psalms 76:2
segments: Salem; the ancient anme, as is generally believed, of Jerusalem, signifying peace.

entries.title: Psalms 76:3
segments: The arrows of the bow; weapons of war.

entries.title: Psalms 76:4
segments: Than the mountains of prey; mountains inhabited by beasts of prey, here used figuratively to represent the warlike heathen nations. Compare

entries.title: Psalms 76:5
segments:
They have slept their sleep; the sleep of death; as was the case with the Assyrians, when a hundred and eighty-five thousand were killed in a night. 
 
  Found their hands; been able to use them.

entries.title: Psalms 76:6
segments:
A dead sleep; the sleep of death. 
 
Without the sustaining care of Jehovah no one can live, and when he ceases to support them his enemies sleep the sleep of death.

entries.title: Psalms 76:8
segments: The earth feared; on account of the wrath of Jehovah, as displayed in the salvation of his people and the destruction of their enemies.

entries.title: Psalms 76:10
segments:
Praise thee; be made the occasion of his praise. 
 
  The remainder of wrath shalt thou restrain; or, more literally, with the remainder of wrath shalt thou gird thyself; that is, that thou mayest use it as a weapon against those who indulge in it. 
 
God will not suffer any more of human wrath to exist than he can overrule for the advancement of his glory and the good of his people.

entries.title: Psalms 76:12
segments: Before the power of God, kings and princes are as helpless as the feeblest among their subjects.  At his rebuke they perish with all their hosts.
